{"id":"persona-5s4b.49","title":"FIDO2 attestor asserts Hardware presence and IAA3 for a merely-connected key; JWT claims a touch that never happened","description":"persona-attestors/src/fido2.rs:574-609: enumerate() calls ctap_hid_fido2::get_fidokey_devices() and, for every device found, emits a Claim with assurance: IdentityAssurance::Iaa3 and presence: PresenceLevel::Hardware. The only thing tested is that a device is enumerable over USB HID. No CTAP2 get_assertion is performed, no UP bit is read, no touch is requested. freshness() (fido2.rs:636-641) returns Fresh unconditionally.

SPEC-HIA.md:141 defines the semantics: "UP bit proves physical touch". SPEC-HIA.md:253: "If presence requirements are not met, personad triggers a presence challenge (FIDO2 touch prompt, Hello dialog, etc.) before issuing the SVID. If the challenge cannot be satisfied within the timeout, the RPC returns UNAUTHENTICATED."

Trigger: build with --features fido2, leave a YubiKey plugged in, and have any process call FetchJWTSVID with audience "https://x?persona_require_presence=hardware".

What goes wrong, step by step:
  1. service.rs:120-137 picks this claim as "best" (Iaa3 outranks every other source).
  2. service.rs:146 checks ext.require_presence > claim.presence -> Hardware > Hardware is false, so the requirement passes.
  3. service.rs:162-173 mints a JWT asserting "presence": {"present": true, "attested_by": "fido2", "attested_at": <now>, "present_until": <now+300>} and "identity_assurance": "iaa3".

The daemon signs an attestation that a human physically touched a security key within the last five minutes. No human was involved and the key was never contacted. A relying party gating a privileged operation on persona_require_presence=hardware -- the sudo/PAM and SSH use cases in SPEC-HIA.md:463-492 are built entirely on this -- is defeated by malware on the same machine, which is precisely the property SPEC-HIA.md:463 claims to provide ("Malware cannot touch a hardware key; it cannot get a cert").

This is not the tracked prove() deferral. prove() being unimplemented is fine; what is not fine is enumerate() reporting a presence level that only prove() could establish, and the service issuing a credential on the strength of it.

Fix direction: until CTAP2 get_assertion lands, enumerate() must report presence: PresenceLevel::None (a connected-but-untouched key attests nothing), and the hardware-presence branch in service.rs should return UNAUTHENTICATED rather than silently downgrade.","status":"open","priority":0,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-09-13T20:58:45.0472732Z","created_by":"agent","updated_at":"2026-09-13T20:58:45.0472732Z","labels":["correctness","review"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"persona-5s4b.49","depends_on_id":"persona-5s4b","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-09-13T20:58:45.072780594Z","created_by":"agent","metadata":"{}"}]}

new_value: Implemented in 4698b8a. Claim moved to its own module with private fields; enumerate returns Candidate, prove returns Evidence, Claim::derive is fallible so no evidence means no claim and the daemon declines. All three acceptance criteria verified by execution. .55 fixed by construction: SelfAssertedDomain has no OrgOidc variant, so oidc.rs cannot anchor a trust domain from an unverified iss.
